'''Amir H. Hoveyda''' is an American organic chemist and professor of chemistry at [[Boston College]], and held the position of department chair until 2018.<ref name=HoveydaWebsite>{{cite web
  | title = BCC Faculty - Amir H. Hoveyda
  | publisher = [[Boston College]]
  | url = http://www.bc.edu/schools/cas/chemistry/faculty/hoveyda.html
  | accessdate = 2007-08-25
  | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20070821161651/http://www.bc.edu/schools/cas/chemistry/faculty/hoveyda.html
  | archivedate = 21 August 2007
  | url-status = dead
  }}</ref> In 2019, he embarked as researcher at the Institute of Science and Supramolecular Engineering at [[University of Strasbourg]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.recherche.unistra.fr/index.php?id=29985|title=Université de Strasbourg - Recherche: La " magie " de la catalyse au service de l'environnement|website=www.recherche.unistra.fr|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

Hoveyda received his Ph.D. from [[Yale University]] under [[Stuart Schreiber]] in 1986, and worked as postdoctoral fellow in the lab of [[David A. Evans]] at [[Harvard University]].<ref name=HoveydaWebsite/> 

He received the Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award from the [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS) in 1998, the ACS Award for Creative Work in Organic Synthesis as well as the [[ENI award]] in 2014,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halford |first=Bethany |date=2025-01-21 |title=ACS Award For Creative Work In Synthetic Organic Chemistry |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/92/i5/ACS-Award-Creative-Work-Synthetic.html |access-date=2026-06-13 |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en}}</ref> and the ACS Herbert C. Brown Award for Creative Research in Synthetic Methods in 2020. In 2011, Hoveyda was ranked among the Top 100 Chemists<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ed |first1=Hayward |title=BC Scientists Ranked Among Top 100 |url=https://www.bc.edu/bc-web/bcnews/news-archive-2011-to-2015/chronicle/2011/news/top100030911.html |agency=BC News |date=9 March 2011}}</ref> in an analysis by [[Thomson Reuters]].

Hoveyda's research focuses on the development for chemoselective and stereoselective catalysis, in particular function-oriented catalyst design. He is particularly noted for his work on developing catalysts for stereoselective [[olefin metathesis]],<ref name="HoveydaSchrock2001">{{cite journal
  | last = Hoveyda
  | first = Amir H.
  |author2=Richard R. Schrock
  |author2-link=Richard R. Schrock
  | title = Catalytic Asymmetric Olefin Metathesis
  | journal = [[Chemistry: A European Journal]]
  | volume = 7
  | issue = 5
  | pages = 945–950
  | pmid = 11303874
  | date = 2001-02-23
  | doi = 10.1002/1521-3765(20010302)7:5<945::AID-CHEM945>3.0.CO;2-3}}</ref> such as the [[Hoveyda–Grubbs catalyst]]. In recent years he has worked extensively on copper(I)-[[N-heterocyclic carbenes]] complex catalyzed allyl addition, allylic substitution and conjugate addition reactions.<ref name="Gillingham2007">{{cite journal
 | author = Gillingham, D. G.
 |author2= Hoveyda, A. H.
 | year = 2007
 | title = Chiral N-Heterocyclic Carbenes in Natural Product Synthesis: Application of Ru-Catalyzed Asymmetric Ring-Opening/Cross-Metathesis and Cu-Catalyzed Allylic Alkylation to Total Synthesis of Baconipyrone C*
 | journal = [[Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. Engl.]]
 | doi = 10.1002/anie.200700501
 | volume = 46
 | pages = 3860–4
 | pmid = 17415730
 | issue = 21
 }}</ref> His research also involves metal-free catalysis, e.g. catalytic stereoselective allyl addition reactions promoted by chiral aminophenol-derived ligands, as well as bioactive molecules synthesis.
